newsitem.title: FRANCE: Feed surplus to probe EU barley export stance.
newsitem.headline: Feed surplus to probe EU barley export stance.

text.p: Growing fears of a feed barley surplus in the European Union have increased expectations that the European Commission will act promptly to cover recent sales to Saudi Arabia, traders and officials said on Monday.

High protein and the risk of pre-germination caused by abnormally wet weather in June have made a significant -- although still unspecified -- proportion of the barley crop unsuitable for domestic brewers this year, the officials said.
Heavy supplies of feed wheat and price competition from alternatives like soya will strengthen perceptions of a domestic feed surplus this year, and could force a softer export stance.
"Even if the Commission wants to hold the line at, say, $150 a tonne (fob), they will have a problem for some time," a European official who closely watches EU export decisions said.
Saudi Arabia last month bought one million tonnes of barley for September and October arrival at prices down to $142 a tonne including freight -- valued by traders at $120 fob.
The EU, the world's largest barley exporter, traditionally adopts a hard line on prices and $150 fob was one recent target.
But Brussels is seen less likely to attempt to defend a strong world price at this stage, given the extra risk of unwanted feed barley landing in EU-controlled intervention.
Feed wheat, which cannot go into intervention, is expected to be especially competitive this year, traders said. Compounders generally prefer it when prices are similar.
The situation is rather severe in Britain where a glut of unexported feed wheat was left over from last season.
Analysts say the EU expects to supply a third of the barley committed to Saudi Arabia but competition will be tougher than expected, with eastern Europe also pushing out heavier crops.
EU tenders for export subsidies officially open on July 17 but officials had previously said there was no hurry to sell.
Barley would need refunds around 25 Ecus a tonne to be sold.
Grain trade association Coceral on Friday predicted an EU feed and malting barley crop of 50.845 million tonnes, down 1.9 percent from last year's unusually large harvest.

But some analysts say the figures may already be out of date and that current fine weather points to a potentially bigger crop. Weather over the next two weeks will be crucial for yields, although some harvesting will be late this year.
